reviewer: Codex author source review; independent approval pending

owner_creation.analysis: src/signal.rs owns notification bits and handler registrations. The module owns sigs and registers image-lifetime handler code; handlers borrow screen/filter/command state owned elsewhere rather than acquiring independent snapshots.
owner_creation.invariant: Registered code lifetime is separate from application state.
limitations: Registering a handler address does not create a snapshot of interrupted owners.

aliases_escapes.analysis: src/signal.rs lets handlers borrow interrupted owners. U_interrupt may retire filter aliases, sigusr1 borrows configuration text then mutates the command queue, and terminate can free owners active on interrupted stacks.
aliases_escapes.invariant: A handler cannot assume interrupted owner borrows ended.
limitations: A suspended filter borrow can be invalidated by u_interrupt.

callback_targets.analysis: src/signal.rs registers concrete application handler targets. Init_signals names u_interrupt, stop, lwinch, terminate, sigalarm and sigusr1; ignored/default/error values still cross Option function-pointer representations.
callback_targets.invariant: Signal sentinels are not ordinary Rust function targets.
limitations: Image-lifetime targets do not resolve the sentinel representation finding.

invalidation.analysis: src/signal.rs cannot reverse effects of an already active handler. Handoff replaces dispositions but active handler work can already have changed filters or queue state; there is no typed retirement token for the registered application context.
invalidation.invariant: Disposition replacement does not restore retired data aliases.

mutation_commit.analysis: src/signal.rs mixes deferred bits with direct handler effects. Sigs uses read/modify/write and psignals snapshots then clears it; some resize work is deferred, while direct filter/queue/quit effects remain outside that commit.
mutation_commit.invariant: Notification bits do not make handler effects transactional.

release_pair.analysis: src/signal.rs releases other owners through filter and quit paths. Set_filter_pattern and quit invoke external owner release; the handlers have no local owning value whose Drop can coordinate those interrupted resources.
release_pair.invariant: Async release must not invalidate suspended ordinary callers.
limitations: Handler-triggered quit may release owners still active on suspended stacks.

error_cleanup.analysis: src/signal.rs does not type signal-registration error sentinels. Registration results are mostly ignored and sentinels are transmuted; fatal handler cleanup can enter an already partial application transaction.
error_cleanup.invariant: Signal error paths lack an independently validated owner state.

signals_handoff.analysis: src/signal.rs retains the four open signal findings. The four maintained M0-SIG findings describe the direct filter mutation, async lookup/queue work, termination cleanup and sentinel representation still left open.
signals_handoff.invariant: Handler review records hazards rather than approving safety.
limitations: This file review reuses current source facts, not a new job-control or signal campaign; no M0-SIG finding is resolved.

src/runtime.rs.relationship: rless_signal at src/runtime.rs:26-41 translates callback and sentinel representations for signal.rs registration. Its returned function-pointer representation remains a separate open ABI concern.
